issues.summary: Minor lint findings: exception re-raised without 'from' and a few long lines.
run-next exits with status 1 when no job is ready, which scripts may read as an error.

issues.evidence: probe p24_add_after_failed_dep_cancelled: add b depending on failed a -> b stays pending forever
issues.summary: A job added with a dependency on a failed or cancelled job stays pending forever and is never cancelled.

issues.evidence: probe p04_id_trailing_newline; B/scheduler.py:13,86 ('^...$' with re.match) accepted id 'abc\n' and persisted it
issues.summary: ID validation accepts a trailing newline because it uses '$' with match instead of fullmatch.

issues.evidence: scheduler.json with priority "x" -> run-next prints 'TypeError: bad operand type for unary -' traceback
issues.summary: load() checks only that keys exist, not their types or ranges, so a malformed state file crashes with a traceback.

issues.evidence: static/B-ruff.txt (28 findings: UP031, E501, C901 run, B904)
issues.summary: Uses %-formatting throughout, and one large run() dispatcher is flagged as too complex.

blinding_guess.why: B ships a .gitignore referencing '.forgemyspec/' state directories and a test suite, which suggests a spec-driven workflow.

notes: Bandit reports for both sides are empty and no security-relevant code (subprocess, eval, pickle) exists in either side. B has no direct cycle-detection gap: cycles cannot normally form through add because dependencies must already exist; p09 uses a pre-seeded dangling dependency, and A rejects that state file outright at load time while B's would_create_cycle catches the cycle. B's tests needed unittest because pytest is not installed; all 11 passed. Neither priority tiebreak (A: insertion order, B: id) is mandated by the spec. A has no tests of its own.
